new_elements: Component: Mechanical clockwork timer knob (retired) — 0-30 min guessing dial with bell, removed because it guesses thaw time.; Component: Reflected-power sensor — Cheap current-sense circuit on the existing magnetron supply that reads absorbed power.; Technology: Dielectric loss sensing — Ice absorbs microwaves poorly and water absorbs them strongly, so absorbed power jumps as food thaws.; Field: Dielectric physics — The physics of how materials absorb microwave energy at different phases.; Function: Stop when food actually thaws — Ends the cycle from the food's own state rather than from a user's guess of minutes.; Function: Ring at true completion — Sounds the end signal only when the food has thawed, so the user never returns to a half-frozen or overcooked meal.
new_edges: Reflected-power sensor -[resolves]-> Mechanical clockwork timer knob (retired); Dielectric loss sensing -[enabled_by]-> Reflected-power sensor; Dielectric physics -[rooted_in]-> Dielectric loss sensing; Reflected-power sensor -[performs_function]-> Stop when food actually thaws; Stop when food actually thaws -[enables_function]-> Ring at true completion; Ring at true completion -[addresses_need]-> M4
rationale: Ending the cycle on detected thaw rather than a guessed time means frozen food finishes in the shortest possible run without the wasted minutes that serve M4 poorly.

title: Load-Matched Power Inverter
anchors: M13 (Energy efficiency)
new_elements: Component: 5-step power knob with duty-cycle cam (original) — Replaced component: a mechanical cam that switches the magnetron on and off in coarse steps regardless of load.; Technology: Solid-state inverter switching — Fast electronic switching that delivers power in fine increments matched to the load.; Component: Load-matched power controller — Sets output from the food's mass and starting temperature, so the magnetron never runs above what the load can absorb.; Function: Deliver only the power the food absorbs — Power is matched to the food, so the unused energy that a fixed-step cam wastes is not generated.

rationale: Matching power to the load stops the magnetron from pushing out energy the food cannot absorb, which is a clear efficiency gain.
judge_comment: Inverter microwaves already exist, but load-matched power control gives a real efficiency gain, though magnetron absorption is hard to sense and the claim is partly overstated.

new_elements: Component: Directional coupler with magnetron anode-current sensor — Measures forward and reflected RF power and anode current to infer the dielectric loss of the load in real time.; Technology: Reflected-power dielectric-loss sensing — Ice has low microwave loss while liquid water has high loss, so the change in reflected power marks the ice-to-water transition.; Function: Detects the ice-to-liquid transition and ends the defrost cycle — Stops or lowers power when the load's loss rises, preventing cooked edges and superheated pockets.

title: Solid-State Phased Array Replaces Magnetron and Turntable
anchors: M4 (Defrost frozen food quickly)

rationale: Solid-state beam steering evens out heating across a frozen block without moving parts, so it defrosts faster and more evenly than a magnetron with a turntable.
judge_comment: Solid-state RF with phase control is real and in development (e.g., commercial products), and it directly improves defrost uniformity, though it is less radical because it is already known.

anchors: glass_turntable (not in graph); clockwork_timer_knob (not in graph); M8 (Human need for feedback (know when food is ready))
new_elements: Component: Load-cell turntable platter — Strain-gauge load cells replace the glass turntable support, reading the food's mass continuously.; Function: Mass loss as doneness proxy — Water loss during heating follows a predictable mass curve, which the controller uses to estimate when the food is ready.; Technology: Load cell with thermal compensation — Load cells compensate for thermal drift, which matters because the platter also warms.
new_edges: Load-cell turntable platter -[performs_function]-> Mass loss as doneness proxy; Mass loss as doneness proxy -[addresses_need]-> M8; Load-cell turntable platter -[resolves]-> glass_turntable; Load-cell turntable platter -[resolves]-> clockwork_timer_knob; Load cell with thermal compensation -[enabled_by]-> Load-cell turntable platter
rationale: Measuring how much water the food has lost gives the user a direct, quantitative readiness signal without any time guess.
judge_comment: Mass loss is a real but noisy proxy for doneness, and load cells under a rotating platter in a microwave are hard to build, so it works for some foods only.

title: Thermally conductive ceramic plate replacing the glass turntable

title: Bakery Breath

title: Impedance Chef

title: Latent-Heat Battery Replaces the Magnetron

title: Magnetron waste-heat recovery loop replaces the cooling fan
anchors: C1 (Magnetron tube (2.45 GHz, ~700 W output)); C7 (Enamelled steel cooking cavity (~20 L)); X2 (FCC/FDA radiation-leakage safety limits (21 CFR 1030.10, 5 mW/cm² at 5 cm))

title: Printed patch array replaces the waveguide

title: Ohmic Thaw Electrodes

title: Sonic Cavity: Acoustic Doneness Sensing Replaces the Lamp

new_elements: Component: Stainless steel electrode tray — Two or more insulated stainless electrodes in the cavity floor that pass low-voltage current through the food.; Function: Ohmic heating of partially thawed food — Heats the food directly by electrical resistance once ice has melted enough to conduct, producing even heating across the load.; Technology: Ohmic (resistive) heating — Joule heating of food by current passing through its conductive liquid phase.; Field: Electrical engineering and food processing — Field from which ohmic heating is drawn.
new_edges: Stainless steel electrode tray -[performs_function]-> Ohmic heating of partially thawed food; Ohmic heating of partially thawed food -[addresses_need]-> M4; Ohmic (resistive) heating -[enabled_by]-> Ohmic heating of partially thawed food; Ohmic (resistive) heating -[rooted_in]-> Electrical engineering and food processing; Stainless steel electrode tray -[resolves]-> microwave_base_v1:glass_turntable

judge_comment: Ohmic heating of food is real, but electrodes in a microwave cavity cause arcing and safety problems, and frozen food does not conduct.

title: Chipless RF tag on packaging replaces power knob

title: Phased-Array Feed Without Turntable

title: Phased-Array Feed Replaces the Turntable
anchors: glass turntable (not in graph)
new_elements: Component: Phased-array RF feed grid — Multiple fixed antennas steer the microwave field electronically so the food heats evenly without any moving parts.; Function: Even field distribution without rotation — Hot and cold spots are removed by beam steering instead of a motor-driven plate.; Technology: Phased-array beam steering — Electronic control of the phase of several RF sources so the field can be aimed.; Field: Antenna engineering — Design of radiating arrays and electromagnetic field shaping.

title: Cooling ticks replace the chime
need_label: Human need for feedback (know when food is ready)

title: Cavity as dielectric sensor
need_label: Human need for feedback (know when food is ready)
anchors: M8 (Human need for feedback (know when food is ready)); base_product:clockwork_timer_knob (not in graph)
new_elements: Component: Feed-port directional coupler with pulsed 2.45 GHz probe — A coupler on the magnetron feed sends low-power probe pulses into the cavity and reads the reflected signal.; Function: Estimate food dielectric state from reflected power — Changes in reflected power and phase track the food's permittivity, which changes as it heats and dries.; Function: Select power and stop time automatically — The dielectric estimate sets the power level and ends cooking at the target state.; Technology: Reflectometry and dielectric spectroscopy of foods — Reflected-signal analysis, calibrated against known foods, gives a dielectric signature for each state.; Field: RF and microwave engineering — Waveguide feeds, couplers, and reflectometry.; Constraint: Cavity load changes with food position and container — Dish placement and container material alter the reflection, so the sensor needs calibration and a position-independent model.

title: Heat-pipe loop replaces the exhaust fan and feeds a water pre-heat tank

title: Motorless Field Rotation Replaces the Turntable
anchors: M13 (Energy efficiency)

title: Magnetron Waste-Heat Recovery Store

title: Thermal-mass tray conducts heat into frozen food

new_elements: Technology: Microwave-absorbing ceramic-graphite thermal mass — A dense tray absorbs microwave energy, stores it, and conducts it into the food by contact.; Component: Heat-storing conductive tray — Replaces the glass turntable; it heats evenly and acts as a thermal flywheel that continues warming the food after the field is off.; Function: Conductive second-stage thawing — Transfers stored heat to the underside of frozen food, reaching the parts the standing-wave field misses.

rationale: Conduction from a heat-storing tray fills in the cold spots that standing waves leave in frozen blocks, so the whole load thaws in less total time.
judge_comment: A susceptor-style heat-storing tray could fill in cold spots, though it would absorb energy that would otherwise go into the food and may not speed up defrosting.

title: Load-Sensing Thaw Electrode

new_elements: Component: NFC tag printed on the food packaging — Passive tag that stores a thaw recipe for the food's weight, type and frozen state.; Technology: Near-field communication program download — The oven reads the tag and loads the matching defrost power curve and stop point.; Function: Selects the correct defrost curve for each package automatically — Removes manual power and time choices, which are the main source of thawing errors.

title: Susceptor Thaw Sleeve

title: Susceptor Sleeve Defrosts Ice by Conduction

new_elements: Component: Removable low-loss ceramic dielectric sleeve — A nested insert narrows the 20 L chamber to the food's footprint so that field energy is not spent on empty volume.; Technology: Low-loss alumina ceramic dielectric lensing — Low-loss ceramics shape and concentrate the RF field onto the food volume.; Function: Concentrate field on food volume only — Reduces the empty cavity the field must fill, so less energy is stored and lost in the chamber walls.

rationale: Concentrating the field on the food rather than the empty 20 L cavity means less energy is wasted filling and heating empty space, which serves M13.
judge_comment: A concentrating dielectric insert is unusual, but ceramics absorb and detune the field and the claimed savings are questionable, as the load rather than the empty cavity absorbs most power.

title: Adaptive resonant cavity with sliding RF shutters

rationale: Shrinking the resonant volume to the food means less RF energy is stored in empty space and lost in the walls, so the same food is heated with less input energy.

title: Phased-Array Field Steering Replaces the Turntable
anchors: base_product:glass_turntable (not in graph); base_product:turntable_motor (not in graph); M13 (Energy efficiency)

rationale: Electronic field steering removes the motor and its standby losses, and uniform heating reduces the need for reheating.

title: Magnetron Echo Readiness Sense

title: Phased-Array Feed replacing the Turntable
anchors: M13 (Energy efficiency); glass turntable (not in graph); turntable motor (not in graph)

title: Thermal Savings Bank in the Walls
anchors: M13 (Energy efficiency)

title: Steam-Bloom Window Coating

title: Scent Cue Vent

title: Acoustic emission sensing replaces the interior lamp

title: Phase-change thermal platen

title: Thermoelectric recovery of magnetron waste heat to power the controls

new_elements: Component: Phase-change thermal battery — Sealed paraffin or salt-hydrate block in the base that absorbs magnetron heat and releases it later.; Technology: Latent heat storage — Stores heat in a material's phase change, which holds far more energy than sensible heating.; Field: Thermal energy storage — Engineering of materials and systems that store and release heat on demand.; Function: Waste-heat recovery and reuse — Captures the magnetron heat that is normally exhausted and returns it to preheat the next load or water.; Constraint: Discarded magnetron waste heat — Roughly a third of input power leaves the magnetron as heat that a cooling fan throws away.
new_edges: Phase-change thermal battery -[resolves]-> base_product:magnetron_cooling_fan; Phase-change thermal battery -[enabled_by]-> Latent heat storage; Latent heat storage -[rooted_in]-> Thermal energy storage; Phase-change thermal battery -[performs_function]-> Waste-heat recovery and reuse; Waste-heat recovery and reuse -[addresses_need]-> M13; base_product:magnetron -[causes]-> Discarded magnetron waste heat; Phase-change thermal battery -[partially_mitigates]-> Discarded magnetron waste heat
rationale: Storing magnetron waste heat in a phase-change battery and reusing it for the next heating cycle recovers energy that the current fan simply exhausts.
judge_comment: Creative, but the waste heat is low-grade, hard to reuse for the next load, and adds cost and complexity, so net savings are doubtful.

title: Magnetron heat pipe feeds a water-preheat reservoir

rationale: Turning the magnetron's waste heat into preheated water cuts the fan's power draw and recovers energy that would otherwise be lost.

title: Motor-free quadrature magnetron feed replaces the turntable drive

title: Thermoelectric harvesting of magnetron waste heat powers standby electronics
anchors: magnetron (not in graph); cooling fan (not in graph)

judge_comment: Ultrasonic thawing exists in labs, but airborne or plate coupling into a frozen block is inefficient and cannot match microwave speed.

anchors: microwave_base_v1 (not in graph); M4 (Defrost frozen food quickly)

new_elements: Component: Connected thaw scheduler — Wi-Fi module that starts the thaw so it finishes when the user is due home, replacing the dial.; Function: Finishes thaw at arrival time — Makes frozen food ready on arrival, so the perceived defrost time is zero.; Technology: Wi-Fi / IoT connectivity — Low-cost wireless link to a phone app or calendar.; Field: Connected appliances — Consumer IoT and scheduling software.; Component: Mechanical clockwork timer — 0-30 minute knob with a bell at the end of the cycle.

rationale: Scheduling the thaw to end at the user's arrival time reframes defrosting as something that happens while they are away, so the need for speed disappears from the user's experience.
judge_comment: Scheduling is easy to build but only hides the wait, and thawing food while nobody is home raises safety concerns.

title: Off-cavity LED light pipe through the sub-cutoff door screen
anchors: interior incandescent lamp (20-25 W) (not in graph); perforated door screen (not in graph)
new_elements: Component: PMMA light pipe — Acrylic light guide passes through a perforated door screen whose holes are far below the 2.45 GHz cutoff, carrying light into the cavity.; Component: 0.3 W white LED driver — Low-power LED mounted outside the metal cavity, so it adds no interior heat and no RF exposure.; Function: Illuminate cavity without internal heat load — Provides the same visibility as the lamp while drawing about 1% of its power and dissipating nothing inside the oven.; Technology: Sub-cutoff perforated metal optics — Microwave-tight screen that transmits visible light through holes much smaller than the RF wavelength.; Constraint: Continuous 20-25 W standby lamp load — The incandescent lamp draws power and heats the cavity even when no cooking is happening.
new_edges: PMMA light pipe -[resolves]-> interior incandescent lamp (20-25 W); 0.3 W white LED driver -[performs_function]-> Illuminate cavity without internal heat load; PMMA light pipe -[performs_function]-> Illuminate cavity without internal heat load; Illuminate cavity without internal heat load -[addresses_need]-> M13; PMMA light pipe -[enabled_by]-> Sub-cutoff perforated metal optics; interior incandescent lamp (20-25 W) -[causes]-> Continuous 20-25 W standby lamp load; 0.3 W white LED driver -[partially_mitigates]-> Continuous 20-25 W standby lamp load
rationale: Removing the 20-25 W interior lamp and running an external 0.3 W LED through a microwave-tight light pipe keeps the cavity visible while cutting lighting energy by roughly 98% and removing heat from the cavity.
judge_comment: Technically sound, but the lamp only runs during cooking, so the savings are small, and modern ovens already use LEDs. It also only partly fits the substitute operator.

title: Switch-mode GaN high-frequency HV supply replaces mains transformer and capacitor stack
anchors: C2 (High-voltage transformer); C3 (High-voltage capacitor (~1 µF, 2.1 kV) with internal bleeder resistor); C4 (High-voltage rectifier diode); T2 (Magnetic-shunt leakage HV transformer); T3 (Half-wave voltage doubler (capacitor + diode)); X7 (HV capacitor can hold a lethal charge after unplugging); X15 (Regional mains variants (230 V/50 Hz vs 120 V/60 Hz))
new_elements: Component: GaN high-frequency switch-mode HV converter (100 kHz) — Rectifies mains to DC, then switches at about 100 kHz into a small ferrite step-up transformer and voltage multiplier to produce 4 kV DC.; Technology: High-frequency switch-mode power conversion — Wide-input PFC stage and resonant GaN converter replace the 50/60 Hz transformer, so the converter works from 120 V or 230 V.; Function: Mains-agnostic, low-energy-storage HV supply — Small stored energy means the HV bus discharges within milliseconds of unplugging, and the same unit runs on both mains standards.
new_edges: GaN high-frequency switch-mode HV converter (100 kHz) -[resolves]-> C2; GaN high-frequency switch-mode HV converter (100 kHz) -[resolves]-> C3; High-frequency switch-mode power conversion -[enabled_by]-> GaN high-frequency switch-mode HV converter (100 kHz); High-frequency switch-mode power conversion -[performs_function]-> F2; Mains-agnostic, low-energy-storage HV supply -[partially_mitigates]-> X7; Mains-agnostic, low-energy-storage HV supply -[partially_mitigates]-> X15; Mains-agnostic, low-energy-storage HV supply -[enables_function]-> F2; Mains-agnostic, low-energy-storage HV supply -[addresses_need]-> M4
rationale: A dependable, regionally portable supply with an instant-discharge bus keeps defrost power available on any mains supply and removes the lethal-charge hazard a parent would otherwise face.
judge_comment: A switch-mode HV supply is feasible and already used in inverter microwaves, but it barely addresses defrost speed.

title: Phone-Pinged Readiness
need_label: Human need for feedback (know when food is ready)
anchors: M8 (Human need for feedback (know when food is ready)); base_product: bell at end of timer (not in graph)
new_elements: Component: Bluetooth Low Energy radio module — A small BLE chip on the control board that pushes readiness events and progress percentages to the user's phone.; Technology: Low-energy Bluetooth (BLE) advertising — A standard low-power wireless protocol that needs no cloud service and works with a phone app.; Function: Remote readiness notification — The user is alerted at any distance in the home, so the food can be checked without standing by the appliance.; Constraint: Magnetron noise and metal cavity impair radio reception — The radio must be shielded and placed outside the cavity to keep its link reliable while the magnetron runs.

rationale: It carries the readiness signal to wherever the user is, so the user does not need to hear a bell or stay in the kitchen.

title: Ice-Block Salt-Brine Sleeve Stirring
anchors: C7 (Enamelled steel cooking cavity (~20 L)); C5 (Waveguide duct); X11 (Cavity volume limited by countertop size); X3 (Uneven heating — standing-wave hot and cold spots)
new_elements: Component: Stirring-vane metal mode stirrer — Rotating-free conductive vanes in the cavity ceiling that continuously reshape the standing-wave pattern.; Technology: Mode-stirring electromagnetic scattering — Scatters the RF field so every part of the frozen block sees a more uniform field over time.; Function: Uniform field distribution without turntable — Spreads energy across the cavity so frozen food thaws evenly with no cold spots.

title: Weight Dial Replaces the Power Knob with Rest Pulses
anchors: C14 (Power-level knob (5-step duty-cycle cam switch)); F8 (Sets average heating power level); X6 (Power only adjustable by on/off cycling, not continuously)
new_elements: Component: Frozen-weight dial — A dial that asks for the food's weight or type instead of a power level, and sets the duty cycle automatically.; Technology: Pulse-and-rest duty cycling — Short bursts followed by rest periods let heat equalise inside the frozen mass and prevent edges from cooking.; Function: Chooses the pulse-and-rest pattern from the food's mass — Converts a technical choice into a simple one the parent can make at a glance.

title: Doneness Hum
need_label: Human need for feedback (know when food is ready)
anchors: M8 (Human need for feedback (know when food is ready))
new_elements: Component: Base: clockwork timer bell — Mechanical bell that rings once at the end of a fixed countdown, with no sense of how the food is doing.; Component: Pitch-glide hum emitter — The transformer and magnetron hum rises or falls in pitch as moisture leaves the food, so the sound itself tracks progress.; Technology: Acoustic signature of moisture loss — Changing load on the magnetron alters its acoustic output, which can be read by ear with no added speaker.; Function: Ambient sense of cooking progress — Lets the user hear how close the food is to ready while they are in another room.

rationale: Progress becomes audible as a continuous pitch change rather than a single bell, so the user knows roughly how far along the food is without checking it.
judge_comment: An audible pitch glide is novel and gives ambient feedback, but magnetron hum does not track moisture loss reliably and the mechanism is vague.

title: Door Latch Piezo Harvester Replaces Controller Standby Supply
anchors: C-door-push-release (not in graph); C-control-electronics (not in graph)
new_elements: Technology: Piezoelectric energy harvesting from mechanical actuation — Converts the mechanical energy of pressing the release button or closing the door into a small electrical charge.; Component: Piezo stack in door latch with supercapacitor — Stores harvested charge to power the timer, display and sensors, removing the standby draw of the control circuit.; Function: Power control electronics without mains standby — Keeps the control logic alive between uses with energy harvested from normal user interaction.

title: Ultrasonic Core Agitator
anchors: microwave_base_v1 (not in graph); M4 (Defrost frozen food quickly)
new_elements: Component: Ultrasonic transducer pad — A small piezo pad in the base that generates internal heat in frozen food, supplementing the magnetron at lower cost than a second heating source.; Technology: Piezoelectric ultrasonic heating — High-frequency acoustic vibration warms the food's interior directly.; Function: Interior core heating — Heats the centre of frozen blocks where microwaves penetrate poorly.

rationale: Heating the core acoustically complements microwave penetration limits, so frozen blocks thaw through their centre much faster.
judge_comment: Ultrasonic core heating is novel, but air-coupled piezo pads cannot transfer meaningful energy into frozen food, so it is largely implausible.

title: Spiked Ice-Pin Platter Replaces the Glass Turntable
anchors: microwave_base_v1 (not in graph); M4 (Defrost frozen food quickly)
new_elements: Component: Conductive ice-pin platter — The glass turntable is replaced by a rotating platter studded with short stainless pins that pierce the frozen block and carry energy into its centre.; Function: Increase thaw surface area — Pins expose the frozen interior to field energy, so the block thaws from the inside as well as the outside.; Technology: Stainless micro-pin machining — Pins are cheap to stamp and sheath in food-safe coating.

rationale: Pinning the ice speeds thawing by reaching the frozen core instead of waiting for heat to travel inward, directly shortening the time to defrost.
judge_comment: Metal pins inside a microwave risk arcing and are hard to insert into frozen food, so it is wild but unsafe.

title: Shrinking Cavity: Only Heat the Space You Use
anchors: glass turntable (not in graph)
new_elements: Component: Sliding ceramic cavity walls — Two or more moveable side panels that reduce the cavity to fit a small portion.; Technology: Low-power servo positioning — Small motors that move the panels to match the chosen portion size.; Function: Concentrate the field on the food — Keeps the microwave energy within the volume that holds the food, so less of it is spent heating empty air and walls.

title: Phased-array antenna replaces turntable motor and roller ring
anchors: C12 (Turntable motor (~5 rpm)); C11 (Roller ring and coupler (turntable support)); C10 (Rotating glass turntable tray); F5 (Distributes heat evenly by rotating food through the field)

title: Phase-change thermal battery tray stores heat for slow release

title: Acoustic Pre-Thaw Chamber

title: Magnetron Song

title: Packaging Is the Timer

title: Kinetic-Harvest Door Latch

title: Thermochromic Doorlight

title: Glow Tray

title: Thermal-reflective stainless walls replace enamelled steel cavity
anchors: C7 (Enamelled steel cooking cavity (~20 L)); T17 (Enamel / epoxy powder coating of steel); X11 (Cavity volume limited by countertop size)
new_elements: Component: Aerogel-insulated double-wall cavity with polished stainless liner — Polished inner wall reflects RF and the evacuated or aerogel-filled outer layer slows heat loss from the cavity to the room.; Technology: Aerogel thermal insulation — Nanoporous silica insulation with very low thermal conductivity, thin enough to fit the existing wrapper.
new_edges: Aerogel-insulated double-wall cavity with polished stainless liner -[resolves]-> C7; Aerogel-insulated double-wall cavity with polished stainless liner -[enabled_by]-> Aerogel thermal insulation; Aerogel-insulated double-wall cavity with polished stainless liner -[performs_function]-> F4; Aerogel thermal insulation -[addresses_need]-> M13; Aerogel-insulated double-wall cavity with polished stainless liner -[partially_mitigates]-> X11
rationale: Insulating the cavity so that less heat escapes into the kitchen and the oven's own enclosure reduces the energy wasted in each cook and lowers the residual heat that a user has to vent.
judge_comment: Insulating the cavity is straightforward, but microwave cook cycles are short so heat loss is minor, and the aerogel and vacuum wall adds cost while the idea's description is somewhat confused.

title: Waveguide-free direct antenna coupling replaces the waveguide duct and mica cover
anchors: C5 (Waveguide duct); C6 (Mica waveguide cover); F3 (Guides microwave energy into the cavity)
new_elements: Technology: Coaxial probe coupling into the cavity — A short coax probe couples RF straight into the cavity, avoiding the metal duct and its losses.; Component: Coaxial feed probe with ceramic seal — A small sealed probe replaces the duct and mica cover, with a ceramic seal to keep splatter out.; Function: Couples RF into the cavity with minimal reflection — Impedance-matched probe delivers energy to the cavity with negligible guiding loss.

title: Ambient Thaw Tray With Warm Air Shell
anchors: M4 (Defrost frozen food quickly)
new_elements: Component: Insulated cavity with passive warm air — A well-insulated cavity that recirculates the warm air already around the food, replacing the 700 W magnetron output with a 60-80 W fan and heater.; Function: Keeps warmth around the food with minimal energy — Slow, gentle convection that thaws the outside first and then the centre without cooking the edges.; Constraint: High wattage is costly and fast to cook edges — 700 W output causes uneven results and high energy use for simple thawing.

rationale: Gentle warm-air convection in a well-insulated cavity avoids the cooked-edge problem and cuts cost, while still thawing frozen food reliably.

title: Thermal Conduction Plate Replaces Turntable

title: Thaw Progress Door Ring
anchors: P1 (Basic countertop microwave oven (timer knob, power knob, door button, lamp)); X9 (Superheating of liquids — risk of eruptive boiling); M4 (Defrost frozen food quickly)

title: Ceramic dielectric probe feed replaces the waveguide and mica cover
anchors: C5 (Waveguide duct); C6 (Mica waveguide cover); F3 (Guides microwave energy into the cavity); M13 (Energy efficiency)
new_elements: Component: Alumina-ceramic dielectric probe antenna — Low-loss ceramic-loaded coaxial probe couples RF from the magnetron directly into the cavity.; Technology: Coaxial probe coupling with low-loss dielectric loading — Direct coupling avoids the TE10 duct and its sealing cover, lowering insertion loss.

rationale: Replacing the waveguide and mica cover with a low-loss direct probe reduces RF transmission losses between the magnetron and the food, so more of the magnetron's output reaches the load.
judge_comment: Waveguide losses are already small, and a ceramic probe handling kW-level RF near the load risks arcing and heating, so the gain is marginal.

title: Cavity-shrink insert replaces empty air volume
anchors: C7 (Enamelled steel cooking cavity (~20 L)); X11 (Cavity volume limited by countertop size); F4 (Heats food via dielectric water-molecule vibration (FastHeating))
new_elements: Component: Microwave-transparent food-sized insert — A mica or glass insert that fills most of the unused cavity air, so the field heats only the food zone.; Function: Confines RF energy to the food zone — Limits the heated volume to the food, reducing RF energy absorbed by empty air and walls.

title: Supercapacitor-buffered pulse power replaces continuous transformer supply
anchors: M4 (Defrost frozen food quickly)

title: Capacitor-Free 48 V Bus Power Stage

rationale: Removing the kilovolt capacitor and transformer makes the oven safe and globally portable, so it can be plugged in and used to thaw food anywhere.

title: Progress Glow

title: Ready Chime Replaced by Thaw Hum
